verdict: REVISE, not SHIP. In-process typed FCS hosting (Fable-style) + TransparentCompiler is a viable, now-measured foundation for a Myriad successor: zero-disk-write splice, correct typed field/attribute access, and automatic stale-dependency detection all confirmed by running code. But this validated exactly one of ~5-6 pillars a real successor needs (typed output, comptime/FSI schema evaluation, hygiene, composable pipelines, plugin packaging all untested), and the one real Myriad generator ported (Fields) came back NULL on the headline 'typed beats syntax' claim - typed access changed nothing for a pure structural-echo generator. Not evidence Myriad has evolved; evidence the foundation for a successor doesn't collapse on contact.
note: First quartet under this repo's own experiments/ methodology (see ../README.md, adapted from an ML-training quartet convention in a different repo). Originally run as an untracked scratch spike; artifacts/ was reconstructed and re-verified after the fact (see artifacts/README.md).
